title: Reading Drill — Testing a tool-cleaning station — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing a tool-cleaning station — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The site workshop manager had been asked to investigate workers returning tools before cleaning off dirt in Cairnford. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on dirt on returned tools, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a ten-week comparison, the team used end-of-day checks at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because unusually busy shifts might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a cleaning point by the return box. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
